messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1765552468 — elevated streaming tail latency detected in az1a, auto-paging on-call

marta: I'm paged, investigating. seeing spikes in streaming tail latency and intermittent 502s for some customers.

eng-runtime: telemetry shows higher TCP retransmits and resolver timeouts from a subset of ephemeral hosts in az1a. KV-cache eviction rate also up ~3x.

alex: confirming 5xx spikes correlate with p99 token tail latency on stream endpoints. about 8% of streaming sessions in az1a have >2s tail.

marta: good context. starting targeted mitigations: 1) enable canary fallback to dedicated pools 2) attempt quick DNS TTL reduction for resolver failover 3) monitor errors.

eng-runtime: enabling route-policy `az1a-stream-fallback` at 5% traffic now — fallback to dedicated-usw2a. applying priming for cache to reduce regen pressure.

incident-bot: route-policy az1a-stream-fallback applied by eng-runtime.

support-lead: prepping customer comms for top affected tenants. sending initial notification that we're rerouting their streaming traffic and monitoring. :phone:

alex: digging into resolver metrics — per-resolver query latency jumped; some resolvers show sporadic packet loss. TTL currently 30s. if we lower TTL we can failover faster.

marta: lowering resolver TTL to 10s for az1a via infra change. executing now: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://ttl-10.json`

incident-bot: DNS TTL change submitted by marta.

eng-runtime: heads up — priming on canary caused temporary token rate spike as caches repopulate; observed p99 regressions for ~2 minutes then improving. overall 502s down ~60% since fallback enabled.

marta: current impact summary: ~8% streaming sessions in az1a saw >2s tail before mitigation; total error rate peaked 1.6% and is trending down. customer-visible for a subset of tenants. no evidence of host capacity exhaustion — appears to be network/resolver instability.

marta: on-call handoff to jamal in 20m. jamal, please take lead post-handoff. I'll leave runbook notes in the incident ticket and handover context.

jamal: taking notes. plan if instability persists: drain ephemeral nodes in az1a, shift steady-state traffic to dedicated pools, and coordinate with cloud provider support if route flaps continue. ETA for full mitigation ~40m assuming no new flaps.

product-ops: product & support are aware; support will post updates to customers every 30m. please add any customer-impact phrases we should use.

marta: will post a status update to #status when metrics stable for 10m. leaving a link to graphs and logs in the incident ticket. handing off now.

incident-bot: On-call handoff recorded: from marta -> jamal at 1765552568.

jamal: got it — I'll coordinate drain + routing if needed and confirm when stable.

support-lead: standing by to send customer follow-ups after next metric check. :mailbox_with_mail:

marta: leaving channel, monitoring passive. thanks all.
